reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3) shows W additions improve dynamic strength and plasticity in TiZrMo-based HEAs via dual-phase microstructures, but the specific alloy system (HfZrTiTa0.53) and the proposed mechanism of enhanced dislocation storage and delayed shear localization are not directly supported; E4 describes general strain-rate effects on dislocation storage that partially align with the mechanism, while E1 notes that aggregated precipitates (W13) degrade properties, which the hypothesis acknowledges as a risk.
premises: Adding ~10 at.% W to HfZrTiTa0.53 forms fine, uniformly dispersed W-rich precipitates
W-rich precipitates act as strong nanoscale obstacles, enhancing dislocation pinning and storage
Enhanced dislocation storage increases work hardening rate under dynamic loading
Increased work hardening delays shear localization and adiabatic softening
These effects improve dynamic uniform elongation and resistance to rapid failure
